messages:

Subject: MSA + Order Form — Term & Renewal questions

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Procurement here at Tesseract has two quick asks before we move to lawyers:

- Auto-renew: We are not comfortable with automatic renewal without an explicit opt-in. Can Redwood remove auto-renew or change to an opt-in renewal confirmation 30–60 days prior to the anniversary?
- Termination for convenience: We need clearer exit mechanics and a reasonable notice window (we usually ask for 60 days). Also want a commitment on data handoff and a short transition assistance period.

If you can share what you’d accept commercially (notice windows, any early-termination fee, pro-rated credits), procurement can route to legal for final redlines. Attaching our suggested term summary for context (Tess-MSA-Terms-request.pdf).

Best,
Lisa

Thanks Lisa — looping in Legal (Laura) and Commercial (Karthik) to align quickly. High level from a sales/ops perspective:

- We prefer maintaining auto-renew for committed contracts because it stabilizes capacity planning, but we can be flexible on notice windows and add explicit renewal notifications.
- For pilots, we’re usually OK removing auto-renew and having a fixed end date.
- Termination for convenience is negotiable if we get clear guardrails around notice timing and a modest early-termination fee for committed capacity.

Laura — can you propose wording that balances our SRE/operational exposure (capacity commitments, offboarding tasks) with their procurement ask? Karthik — what commercial concessions would help close this if they insist on removing auto-renew?

I’ve put a short stopgap addendum draft attached that preserves the core MSA but offers a 45-day notice as an opening offer (stopgap-addendum-draft.docx).

Next steps: legal redline + commercial counter if needed, then a single doc back to Tesseract for their legal review.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — Term & Renewal questions

Vanessa / Lisa — thanks for the context. Attached is a legal-proposed redline of the MSA focused on Term, Renewal, and Termination for Convenience (MSA_Term_Redline_20260929.docx). Summary of material points in plain English:

1) Auto-renewal: keep auto-renew for committed orders but add an explicit renewal notice obligation and a 30-day cure window. For pilot order forms we will include a non-renewing fixed term.

2) Notice window: propose 45 days for standard contracts (middle ground). If Customer requires 60 days, we can accept but will require a 3-month minimum committed capacity or a modest early-exit fee to cover scheduling/GC migration costs.

3) Termination for convenience: allow with 60 days' notice and pro-rated refund for unused prepaid amounts when termination is initiated by Customer, but carve out committed reserved capacity (outstanding committed spend) where a termination fee applies. Also add an express data export and handoff SLA (30 days), and an implementation offboarding checklist to be appended to the Order Form.

4) Transition assistance: flat-rate Transition Assistance fee or up to X hours at list to cover knowledge transfer and runbook handoff; alternative is limited complimentary assistance if Customer migrates to another Redwood product within 30 days (commercially defensible tradeoff).

5) Clean-up language: process for how the order form termination interacts with Standing Orders / Dedication (i.e., what happens to reserved pools).

I’ve included in the redline a few optional clauses (marked) so commercial can pick the preferred tradeoff. If Tesseract wants removal of auto-renew entirely, the commercial team should be ready to offer a one-time onboarding credit or price concession.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Quick commercial note: if Customer insists on removing auto-renew for a multi-year committed order, we can offer either:

- a 12% onboarding/commitment credit applied over the first 3 months (one-time), or
- keep auto-renew but increase notice window to 60 days and offer a 10% discount on committed GPU rate for the first year.

For pilots (non-committed), let’s remove auto-renew and ship a non-renewing order form. For committed deals, prefer to preserve auto-renew but accept Laura’s 45-day default if we sweeten with the discount above.

If agreed, I can reflect the chosen commercial option in the counter-order form and mark the HubSpot deal as "pending legal acceptance".

— Karthik

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — Term & Renewal questions

Lisa — thanks, all. Quick summary and proposed path forward so procurement has a single source of truth: 

1) Pilot: non-renewing order form (no auto-renew). Tesseract confirmed pilot dates in our prior thread; we’ll ship a fixed-term pilot OF.
2) Committed: keep auto-renew but add explicit renewal notice (45 days) + data handoff SLA and 60-day handoff target post-termination. If Tesseract requires 60-day notice instead of 45, Redwood will provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 12% of first-year committed spend (applied over first 3 months).
3) Termination for convenience: allowable with pro-rated refund for prepayments, but committed reserved capacity will be subject to an early-termination fee (per the redline). We’ll append the implementation/offboarding checklist to the Order Form.

Deliverables & timing:
- Laura to send final marked redline (done) and a clean clause set for insertion into the OF (by EOD today).
- Commercial to prepare counter-Order Form reflecting the chosen commercial tradeoff (Karthik) — I asked for the 12% credit option as our standard concession if Tesseract insists on 60-day notice.
- I will send the single countersigned OF back to procurement with the offboarding checklist and a DocuSign link.

Lisa — if that flow works for procurement, I’ll queue the docs now and target sending the counter by close of business today. Please confirm and I’ll route to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
